tagline: Farmland, a crossroads town and open ground preserved for horse racing
intro: Old Tavern Road crosses farmland on two undivided lanes, linking Old Tavern with The Plains. Numbered Route 245 and designated a Virginia Byway, it runs 3.27 miles from U.S. 17 to Route 55. Farther north, Middleburg’s nineteenth-century town center forms a National Register historic district.

Middleburg lies on the Ashby Gap trading route, midway between Alexandria and Winchester. Leven Powell established the town in 1787. U.S. 50 now follows that trading route, while visitors began coming for foxhunting and steeplechasing in the early 1900s.

Read the journey southward from Middleburg to The Plains, where Routes 55 and 245 meet. From The Plains, Route 245 leaves town as Fauquier Avenue and Old Tavern Road, passing the Interstate 66 interchange. It crosses Piney Branch of Broad Run through farmland before reaching U.S. 17 at Old Tavern.

moments.title: Middleburg
moments.text: Middleburg lies between two destinations: Alexandria’s port and Winchester, linked by the Ashby Gap trading route. Leven Powell established the town in 1787 but declined to have it named for him. Before Middleburg, the settlement’s names included Chinn’s Crossroads and Powell Town, followed by the spelling Middleburgh. The route now carries U.S. 50. In the early 1900s, foxhunting and steeplechasing began drawing visitors to the village. The National Sporting Library researches horse and field sports here. The nineteenth-century center is a historic district on the National Register of Historic Places.

moments.title: The Plains
moments.text: The Plains sits at the meeting of Routes 55 and 245. Maps called the area White Plains before and during the Civil War, while its post office had used The Plains since 1831. The town incorporated in 1910, and most of it entered the National Register as The Plains Historic District in 2014. On Loudoun Avenue near the railway tracks, the Afro-American Historical Association of Fauquier County houses its offices, library, archives and museum exhibit, Footprint to Change. State Route 245 provides the town’s most direct link to Interstate 66.

moments.title: Great Meadow
moments.text: Great Meadow’s open ground was once slated for a development of more than 500 homes. In 1982, news executive and philanthropist Arthur W. Arundel founded Great Meadow and its foundation, donating land when the Virginia Gold Cup needed a new home after losing its Warrenton lease. The 380-acre field events center and steeplechase course is managed by a nonprofit dedicated to preserving open space for community use. Its grounds include four ponds, polo facilities and space for public and private events. The grounds also serve as the home of model rocket launches, including the Team America Rocketry Challenge.
